title: SAXON Q Introduces Patented Quantum Watchdog System for Runtime QPU Fault Detection - Quantum Computing Report
gist: SAXON Q unveiled Quantum Watchdog, a patented hardware-agnostic runtime fault-detection architecture that uses an independent classical processor, environmental telemetry and interleaved test calculations to catch QPU hardware failures or tampering, targeting edge (defense, robotics, automotive) and multi-QPU HPC deployments, with first custom implementations in early 2027.

insights.claim: SAXON Q's Quantum Watchdog is designed to complement quantum error correction by detecting hardware degradation, environmental drift or tampering in quantum processors during live operation, rather than stochastic qubit noise, and moving compromised units into a safe state.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Functional safety is a prerequisite for quantum in regulated edge markets; first-mover patents could create licensing revenue.

insights.claim: Quantum Watchdog targets edge deployments in defense, robotics and automotive environments as well as multi-QPU HPC clusters.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Room-temperature NV-diamond QPUs open edge use cases that cryogenic platforms cannot address.

insights.claim: Quantum Watchdog runs on an independent classical processor with isolated clocks, timers and environmental sensors, monitoring power draw, temperature and ambient magnetic fields while interleaving verified test calculations into user workloads.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Mirrors automotive-style safety architectures, easing certification paths.
insights.locator: Operating on an independent classical processor

insights.claim: Users can allocate up to 50% of QPU runtime to Watchdog diagnostic verification or restrict checks to startup and intermittent intervals.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Safety comes at a potentially significant throughput cost in critical applications.
insights.locator: Operating on an independent classical processor

insights.claim: For multi-core configurations, Quantum Watchdog uses dual-processor comparison or majority voting across three or more processors to isolate and shut down malfunctioning units without halting cluster execution.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Redundancy-based safety increases QPU unit demand per deployment.
insights.locator: Operating on an independent classical processor

insights.claim: Quantum Watchdog will first be offered as a configurable option on SAXON Q's room-temperature SXQ128 and SXQ512 multi-core processors by dedicating an onboard control circuit to safety monitoring, though it is compatible with superconducting, trapped-ion and quantum sensing modalities.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Hardware-agnostic design enables OEM licensing beyond SAXON Q's own NV-diamond hardware.

insights.claim: Quantum Watchdog is protected by granted patents in Europe, the United States and China and is slated for initial custom implementation in early 2027 with OEM and system integrator licensing, with safety-certified versions to follow after independent auditing and field testing.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Watch early-2027 implementations and certification timelines as validation of the licensing model.
